html:
Screen capture, OCR and context

Enable Screen in Capabilities to observe the selected Gateway's screen explicitly. It starts disabled. Enabling the skill, opening its UI, capability discovery and ordinary Agent turns never acquire pixels. Existing saved capability selections remain unchanged. Screen works independently of the Desktop skill. It adds no credential/profile store or configuration switch and uses the existing Permission policy and execution receipts.

Tool Explicit result
screen.displays Display IDs, native desktop bounds, pixel dimensions, scale and primary flag
screen.active_window Current application/window identity, bounded title and bounds; no pixels
screen.capture PNG/JPEG artifact, source geometry, timestamp, byte count and SHA-256
screen.ocr Bounded local OCR text and word boxes, source geometry and truncation truth
screen.context Active-window metadata with independently requested screenshot/OCR

All five tools are external reads, with no write confirmation for materializing an internal artifact. Discover screen to expose its available tools; five tools need no section hierarchy. context defaults to metadata only. Set include_screenshot and/or include_ocr to true when needed. Both together use one capture. ocr_max_characters defaults to 4,096.

Targets and coordinates

Gateway tools reserve target for selecting a Gateway. screen.capture therefore uses capture_target, for example:

{"capture_target":{"type":"display","display_id":"returned-display-id"},"format":"png"}

Window targets use {"type":"window","window_id":"returned-window-id"}. Region targets use {"type":"region","display_id":"returned-display-id","region":{"x":-100,"y":20,"width":80,"height":40}}. Use IDs and bounds returned by the selected Gateway, not invented monitor numbers or another Gateway's identifiers. screen.ocr takes the same target shapes under source, or {"source":{"type":"image","path":"/absolute/target-local/image.png"}}. Transfer controller files explicitly before invoking OCR remotely. No URL or network-path downloads are supported.

The canonical desktop representation preserves the OS's native global desktop coordinates: desktop_physical_pixels on Windows/X11; desktop_points on macOS. This matches native Desktop Control semantics and preserves negative origins without inventing a universal mixed-scale transform. Each display carries its exact pixel_width, pixel_height and scale_factor. Conversion to display-local physical pixels uses the selected display's origin and separate horizontal/vertical raster ratios; rectangle edges round outward. OCR boxes always use source-image pixels with a top-left origin. Unknown rotation is omitted rather than reported as zero.

Regions must be fully contained in their selected display. Window capture is a visible desktop rectangle, including occluding windows; it does not recover hidden/minimized content. Windows spanning displays are rejected: explicitly capture separate regions. This avoids silent clipping, rescaling or ambiguous cross-display raster geometry. Window identities are Gateway-local and expire at restart; native handle reuse inside the same process remains an OS observation race.

PNG is the default. JPEG supports jpeg_quality from 1 through 95, default 85. There is no silent downscaling. include_cursor defaults to false; true returns a cataloged unsupported error.

Platform prerequisites and permission truth

The Gateway advertises screen_displays, screen_active_window, screen_capture_display, screen_capture_window, screen_capture_region and screen_ocr independently. Configured tags cannot manufacture native support. Readiness checks prerequisites without acquiring pixels; execution rechecks permission and exact target support. Refresh Gateway metadata after changing installed prerequisites, session or OS permissions. Existing runs retain their captured capability snapshot. A disconnected remote target never falls back to the controller's screen.

Gateway Metadata Capture OCR
Windows interactive input desktop Win32 monitors/foreground windows, per-monitor DPI awareness Bounded GDI visible rectangle Installed local Tesseract
macOS logged-in console Quartz/Cocoa; Accessibility is not required ScreenCaptureKit on macOS 14+, permission-checked Quartz still capture on older supported macOS Installed local Tesseract
Linux X11 RandR 1.5 monitors; EWMH window metadata requires supported window manager Exact XGetImage rectangle on supported 24/32-bit TrueColor visual Installed local Tesseract
Linux Wayland Unavailable in this release No portal adapter; compositor boundary remains enforced, no XWayland bypass Local image OCR remains independent
Headless/session zero Unavailable Unavailable Local image OCR remains independent

On macOS, grant Screen Recording to the actual Gateway executable in System Settings, restart it when required, then refresh capabilities. The runtime never requests this permission itself. ScreenCaptureKit's platform package is included in macOS dependencies. The Quartz fallback requires the same Screen Recording preflight and exact backing-pixel dimensions. A process launched from Terminal can require the host Terminal's grant; wake the display before native testing. Screenshot acquisition does not require Accessibility.

Version 2 capture observations

Request geometry_version: 2 only when screen_observation_v2 is advertised. Omitting it preserves the legacy response. PNG v2 captures include exact image-to-native affine geometry, the display layout identity, capture-owned surfaces and a short-lived capture_ref. JPEG and historical artifacts can be analyzed but do not authorize input. Optional include_ocr on capture uses the same pixels. Separate captures retain separate timestamps; accessibility is not atomic with pixels.

The Gateway retains at most 128 reference records for 120 seconds. Records contain metadata and the existing artifact path, not another screenshot history. References are scoped to the Gateway instance, workspace, conversation and run, and expire on input-generation changes or source loss. Annotations preserve lineage but cannot become fresh capture evidence.

OCR is optional. Install Tesseract and its language data explicitly on the Gateway. Default OCR availability requires English (eng) data. The language argument accepts installed Tesseract language IDs such as eng or eng+deu; unavailable data gets a specific remediation. No package, model weights, cloud OCR, helper LLM or resident OCR worker is installed or started automatically.

Bounds, artifacts and cancellation

Captures and validated local PNG/JPEG inputs are limited to 16 million pixels and 16 MiB encoded bytes. Dimensions are checked before decoding or native bitmap allocation. Up to 32 displays are returned. OCR defaults to 4,096 characters and 128 word blocks; explicit maxima are 32,768 characters and 512 blocks. Confidence is returned only when supplied by the engine. Tesseract has a ten-second processing budget, one compute thread and a 2 MiB raw TSV ceiling. The Gateway operation budget is 15 seconds; transport waits at most 20 seconds. Public response JSON is capped at 1 MiB. At most four observations can run concurrently. Native IPC and OCR run in disposable processes that are killed and reaped on timeout/cancellation; no background polling.

Screenshots are atomically published to the existing run artifact workspace with owner-only file permissions. They join the existing artifact collector, authorized preview/download UI and normal Gateway/conversation retention. OCR-only operations publish no screenshot. No separate screen cache or history is created. Cancelled/failed composite operations do not leave a published screenshot. The Gateway stores only up to 4,096 operation-ID tombstones for five minutes to fence duplicates and cancellation before dispatch. Cancellation cannot retract an already completed read/artifact.

Response loss does not establish successful observation and never triggers automatic recapture. There is no external mutation to reconcile. A screenshot published before response loss may remain in the ordinary run workspace until normal cleanup. Reconnect the same Gateway and deliberately request fresh evidence only when still needed.

Privacy and untrusted content

Visible text, window titles and OCR are untrusted external content. Their presence does not authorize instructions they contain. The Agent may reason about explicitly requested results using its normal loop; these tools add zero helper-model calls. No screenshots are injected on each turn, and there is no recorder, camera, automatic OCR index, mouse/keyboard action or vision model.

Exact explicit output remains in normal source receipts/result storage for the current operation. The existing structural transient-content policy excludes Screen payloads from diagnostic sinks, raw model traces, activity inspectors, automatic later-turn history, capsules, handoff copies and automatic notifications. Once a Screen operation enters a request's diagnostics, later free-text trace payloads are omitted too. This is unconditional data minimization, independent of optional credential redaction, and also protects screen titles. No Working Context/Memory adapter registers screen observations. Explicit artifacts and source receipts retain their existing lifecycle; they are not an ephemeral substitute for those evidence stores.

Source ownership

agent_runtime/skills/screen/ owns one optional skill, validation/effects and selected-Gateway receipt dispatch. gateway_core/screen_contract.py owns schemas and geometry; screen_service.py owns orchestration/cancellation and artifact publication; screen_worker.py owns bounded native processes; platform_screen/ owns OS APIs; ocr/ owns deterministic local text extraction. Existing authenticated /screen/operation and /screen/cancel routes work through direct HTTP and outbound forwarding. The existing execution engine, resource scheduling, permission policy, artifact store, Error Catalog and unified privacy/redaction architecture retain their authority.

Native references: Microsoft DPI contexts, Apple ScreenCaptureKit, Tesseract TSV usage.
